title: Want to see what denying the Judgement looks like?
subtitle: Belief shows in how you treat people
then: Ibn Kathir says Din here means {idea}the Hereafter, the Recompense and the Final Reward{/idea}. Maududi says the surah shows {trap}what kind of morals a person develops{/trap} when he does not believe he will be held to account.
now: You would never say out loud that there is no Judgement. But watch what you do when nobody important is looking: the delivery driver, the cleaner, the kid nobody claims. {idea}The verse says belief is visible there.{/idea}
old: I believe in the Hereafter. I have never denied it.
new: My belief in the Judgement shows most in how I treat people who cannot repay me.
try: Notice how you treat the least powerful person you meet today. Be a little kinder than usual.

title: He is the one who pushes the orphan away.
subtitle: The first sign of denial
then: Ibn Kathir says he is the one who {trap}oppresses the orphan and does not give him his just due{/trap}. He does not feed him, {trap}nor is he kind to him{/trap}. The orphan had no one to complain to.
now: The relative's child who lost a parent and now gets fewer invitations. The new kid at school nobody sits with. The colleague grieving alone. {idea}Not being cruel is not enough.{/idea} The verse names neglect as pushing away.
old: I have never hurt an orphan. This does not apply to me.
new: Ignoring someone who has no protector is a way of pushing them away.
try: Reach out today to someone who has lost a parent: a call, a meal, a small gift.

title: He does not even urge others to feed the poor.
subtitle: Silence about hunger
then: Ibn Kathir links it to the verse: {trap}you urge not one another to feed the poor{/trap}. The miskin is {idea}the poor man who has nothing to sustain him{/idea}. The verse does not only blame not feeding, but not even encouraging it.
now: You may not have much spare cash this month. But you can share the food-bank link, remind the group about a family in need, ask your workplace to match a donation. {reward}Urging is a deed too.{/reward}
old: I do not have money to spare, so feeding the poor is not my job.
new: Even when I cannot give, I can urge others to give. Staying silent is the problem.
try: Share one way to help feed people in need with a friend or a group chat today.

title: Woe to those who pray. Yes, those who pray.
subtitle: The surprising turn of the surah

row.title: automatic safety
sub: I pray, so I am fine

row.title: it must be real
sub: the rest of the sentence matters

then: After the deniers, the surah turns to {trap}people who actually pray{/trap}. Ibn Abbas and others said this means the hypocrites who pray in public but not in private. Ibn Kathir says they adhere to prayer {idea}yet are mindless of it{/idea}.
now: You pray five times. You might even feel a little proud of it. Then this verse: {trap}woe to those who pray{/trap}. It stops you mid-step. Not to make you stop praying, but to make you ask what kind of praying it is.
old: I pray, so the warnings in this surah are not about me.
new: Praying is not a shield on its own. Allah asks how I pray, not only whether I do.
try: In your next prayer, think about the meaning of just one phrase you recite.

title: Heedless of their prayer, not just distracted in it.
subtitle: The many ways prayer gets neglected
then: Ata' bin Dinar said: {reward}praise be to Allah who said heedless of their prayer, not in their prayer{/reward}. Ibn Kathir lists meanings: neglecting it, delaying it, rushing it. The Prophet ﷺ described a hasty, late prayer where one {trap}does not remember Allah except a little{/trap}.
now: You glance at the clock, realise Asr is nearly gone, and rush four rakahs while thinking about dinner. {reward}Wandering thoughts happen to everyone.{/reward} The verse warns about the habit of not caring, not about the moment your mind drifts.
old: My mind wanders in prayer, so my prayer is worthless.
new: A wandering mind is human. The warning is for treating prayer as unimportant.
try: Set a gentle reminder for one prayer today so you pray it calmly, not rushed.

title: They do good only so that people see.
subtitle: Deeds performed for an audience
then: The Prophet ﷺ said whoever {trap}makes people hear of his deed, Allah will make him heard and degraded{/trap}. Ibn Kathir adds a relief: {reward}whoever does a deed only for Allah and people find out, and he is pleased, that is not showing off{/reward}.
now: The donation receipt you post. The Ramadan night-prayer selfie. The way you mention you fasted Monday. {trap}Who was it for?{/trap} And if someone sees your quiet good deed by accident, relax: that is not riya.
old: If anyone sees my good deeds, they are ruined.
new: What matters is who I did it for. Being seen by chance does not spoil it.
try: Do one good deed today and tell absolutely no one about it.

title: They will not even lend a pot or a bucket.
subtitle: The smallest help, withheld
then: Ibn Mas'ud said al-ma'un is {idea}what people give each other: an axe, a pot, a bucket{/idea}. Ibn Kathir says they {trap}do not worship their Lord well, nor treat His creation well{/trap}, refusing to lend what would be returned intact.
now: Your neighbour asks to borrow the ladder. A classmate wants your notes. A colleague needs your phone charger for ten minutes. {reward}Tiny things that cost you nothing.{/reward} The surah ends here because this is where character shows.
old: Lending small things is a hassle. It is my stuff.
new: Lending a small thing is part of worship. How I treat people and how I pray go together.
try: Offer to lend something today before you are even asked.
